title: Rigveda 1.20: To the Ribhus
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.20: To the Ribhus: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.20 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to the Ribhus. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 10r-10v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.20.1-8 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 2, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 10v
translation.original_text:
1a̱yaṁ de̱vāya̱ janma̍ne̱ stomo̱ vipre̍bhir āsa̱yā | akā̍ri ratna̱dhāta̍maḥ ||
2ya indrā̍ya vaco̱yujā̍ tata̱kṣur mana̍sā̱ harī̍ | śamī̍bhir ya̱jñam ā̍śata ||
3takṣa̱n nāsa̍tyābhyā̱m pari̍jmānaṁ su̱khaṁ ratha̍m | takṣa̍n dhe̱nuṁ sa̍ba̱rdughā̍m ||
4yuvā̍nā pi̱tarā̱ puna̍ḥ sa̱tyama̍ntrā ṛjū̱yava̍ḥ | ṛ̱bhavo̍ vi̱ṣṭy a̍krata ||
5saṁ vo̱ madā̍so agma̱tendre̍ṇa ca ma̱rutva̍tā | ā̱di̱tyebhi̍ś ca̱ rāja̍bhiḥ ||
6u̱ta tyaṁ ca̍ma̱saṁ nava̱ṁ tvaṣṭu̍r de̱vasya̱ niṣkṛ̍tam | aka̍rta ca̱tura̱ḥ puna̍ḥ ||
7te no̱ ratnā̍ni dhattana̱ trir ā sāptā̍ni sunva̱te | eka̍m-ekaṁ suśa̱stibhi̍ḥ ||
8adhā̍rayanta̱ vahna̱yo 'bha̍janta sukṛ̱tyayā̍ | bhā̱gaṁ de̱veṣu̍ ya̱jñiya̍m ||
translation.text:
1FOR the Celestial Race this song of praise which gives wealth lavishly Was made by singers with their lips.
2They who for Indra, with their mind, formed horses harnessed by a word, Attained by works to sacrifice.
3They for the two Nâsatyas wrought a light car moving every way: They formed a nectar-yielding cow.
4The R̥ibhus with effectual prayers, honest, with constant labour, made Their Sire and Mother young again.
5Together came your gladdening drops with Indra by the Maruts girt, With the Âdityas, with the Kings.
6The sacrificial ladle, wrought newly by the God Tvashṭar's hand- Four ladles have ye made thereof.
7Vouchsafe us wealth, to him who pours thrice seven libations, yea, to each Give wealth, pleased with our eulogies.
8As ministering Priests they held, by pious acts they won themselves, A share in sacrifice with Gods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 10v (OPenn image 12, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.20.1 ‹-akāri ratna-dhātamaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 11r, begins in RV 1.21.4 ‹upa idam savanam sutam›. Verses 1.20.1-8 end on this page; 1.20.1 begins on fol. 10r.

1ayam | devāya | janmane | stomaḥ | viprebhiḥ | āsayā | akāri | ratna-dhātamaḥ
2ye | indrāya | vacaḥ-yujā | tatakṣuḥ | manasā | harī iti | śamāībhiḥ | yajñam | āśata
3takṣan | nāsatyābhyām | pari-jmānam | su-kham | ratham | takṣan | dhenum | sabaḥ-dughām
4yuvānā | pitarā | punariti | satya-mantrāḥ | ṛjū-yavaḥ | ṛbhavaḥ | viṣṭī | akrata
5sam | vaḥ | madāsaḥ | agmata | indreṇa | ca | marutvatā | ādityebhiḥ | ca | rāja-bhiḥ
6uta | tyam | camasam | navam | tvaṣṭuḥ | devasya | niḥ-kṛtam | akarta | caturaḥ | punariti
7te | naḥ | ratnāni | dhattana | triḥ | ā | sāptāni | sunvate | ekam-ekam | suśasti-bhiḥ
